newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says Netanyahu, Arafat may meet.
newsitem.headline: Israel says Netanyahu, Arafat may meet.

text.p: Israel said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat discussed on Thursday meeting to end two days of fighting in which 33 people have been killed.

Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh told Israel Radio: "In the discussion the prime minister had with Yasser Arafat the possiblity of their meeting came up. This possibility is on the agenda. There is no conclusion on this matter as yet."
A senior PLO official confirmed that Netanyahu had asked for a meeting as soon as the prime minister returned from a shortened trip to Europe later on Thursday.
Another official, Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, director-general of the Palestinian presidency, told Reuters:

"We are not against a meeting, provided that it is a serious entry into implementing agreements and to stop (Israeli) violations against our people, especially against our holy places (in Jerusalem)."
Palestinian medical officials said 29 Palestinians had been killed in two days of clashes with Israeli troops. Israeli army radio said five Israelis died in fighting on Thursday.
